Meteg after silluq: manuscript images for the verse-final word at Job 4:12

← Back to the case register.

The Aleppo Codex has both strokes at Job 4:12.

The Leningrad Codex has both strokes at Job 4:12.

Cambridge Add. 1753 has a meteg after the silluq at Job 4:12.

We usually regard the position of an “early meteg”—a meteg to the right of its vowel—as meaningless. Yet the stroke under the mem is to the right of its segol in both the Aleppo Codex and the Leningrad Codex. On this page's interpretation, both codices therefore have an “early silluq” here, which seems an extraordinary coincidence. In Cambridge Add. 1753, the silluq under the mem is to the left of its segol, in the normal position.
